data.name: Ishaqah
data.gender_notes: Ishaqah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Ishaqah is the name of Prophet Jacob's wife. Her faithfulness and devotion are celebrated throughout Islamic history. The name Ishaqah carries the meaning “Jacob's wife” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ishaqah usually hope their child will grow to embody jacob's wife and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ishaqah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jacob's wife.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ishaqah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: إسحاقة
in_arabic.meaning: إسحاقة تعني الفتاة التي تتبع إسحق عليه السلام
in_arabic.long_meaning: إسحاقة هي اسم علم مؤنث مشتق من اسم إسحق عليه السلام، ويعني الفتاة التي تتبع إسحق أو تنتمي إليه، وإسحق هو اسم نبي الله إسحق بن إبراهيم عليهما السلام، ويعتبر إسحق شخصية مهمة في التاريخ الإسلامي واليهودي والمسيحي.

in_urdu.name: اسحاقہ

data.cultural_impact: Ishaqah is an Arabic name derived from the root word "ashq" which means "extreme love" or "passion." This name carries a deep cultural significance in the Islamic world, reminding us of one of the most faithful and devoted wives in Islamic history - Prophet Jacob's wife, known as Asiyah or Ishaqah. Her story is a testament to enduring love, loyalty, and commitment between a husband and wife. The name Ishaqah not only reminds us of this beautiful love story but also inspires us to cultivate such virtues in our own relationships.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Ishaqah also holds immense spiritual significance as it represents the purest form of love and devotion to Allah. The name is associated with the story of Prophet Jacob (AS) and his beloved wife Asiyah or Ishaqah. She demonstrated unwavering faith through her trials and demonstrated her love for Allah by being obedient to her husband, Jacob, and strengthening the bond of their marriage. Her steadfastness and dedication serve as an inspiration for Muslims to continually seek a deeper connection with Allah and strive to live in complete submission to His will. The name Ishaqah is a reminder of the transformative power of love, both in the context of personal relationships and our relationship with Allah.
